unDef.description: Which set of identifying columns of a table are chosen for the SPECIAL_COLUMNS_QUERY when there is more than one candidate set.
Whether or not a column a column identified for a given table in SPECIAL_COLUMNS_QUERY is a pseudo-column.
The algorithm used to determine the value of the PSEUDO_COLUMN column in SPECIAL_COLUMNS_QUERY.
The effect on diagnostic information of incompatibilities between the character repertoires supported by the SQL-client and SQL-server.
If multiple status records are generated, then, with two exceptions, the order in which status records are placed in a diagnostics area.
The values to which fields whose values depend on a value of TYPE and fields that are not applicable for a particular value of TYPE are set.
The value to which the descriptor item NAME is set when a column or field name is implementation-dependent.
The four-octet value that represents a locator.
The values of the variables addressed by DATA_POINTER and OCTET_LENGTH_POINTER fields in the item descriptor area when the value of the bound target is NULL.

The values of TYPE, LENGTH, PRECISION, and SCALE fields of the item descriptor area of the implementation parameter descriptor and the TYPE, DATA_POINTER, INDICATOR_POINTER, and OCTET_LENGTH_POINTER fields of the item descriptor area of the allocated CLI descriptor area when BindParameter() raises an exception.
The values of the remaining octets when a string is assigned to target of greater length.
The values of all fields of the item descriptor area, except for COUNT, for which specific values were provided in the invocation of SetDescField() when an exception condition is raised.
The values of every output argument that corresponds to an output parameter of a CLI routine whose value is not explicitly defined by [ISO9075-3].
The values of all bound targets when the the number of rows in a rowset is 0 (zero).

The value of COLUMN_SIZE in COLUMNS_QUERY or SPECIAL_COLUMNS_QUERY when the value of DATA_TYPE in the COLUMNS view is not one of CHARACTER, CHARACTER VARYING, CHARACTER LARGE OBJECT, BINARY, BINARY VARYING, BINARY LARGE OBJECT, DECIMAL, NUMERIC, SMALLINT, INTEGER, BIGINT, REAL, DOUBLE PRECISION, FLOAT, DECFLOAT, DATE, TIME, TIMESTAMP, TIME WITH TIME ZONE, TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, INTERVAL, or REF.
The values of all fields of the item descriptor area, except for COUNT, for which specific values were provided in the invocation of SetDescRec() when an exception condition is raised.
The values of all other output arguments when the IndicatorValue or StrLen_or_Ind argument is set to the value indicating SQL NULL DATA.
The values of all output arguments when the fetched row set of GetData() is empty.
The values of NativeError, MessageText, and TextLength when Error() returns no status record.
The values of the TYPE, OCTET_LENGTH, LENGTH, DATA_POINTER, INDICATOR_POINTER, and OCTET_LENGTH_POINTER fields of the item descriptor area when BindCol() raises an exception condition.
The column name of a derived column that does not specify AS and is neither a single column reference nor single SQL parameter reference.
The default cursor name property associated with an allocated SQL-statement.

The value of ColumnSize when information is retrieved from an implementation row descriptor and the data type of the column is neither exact numeric, approximate numeric, datetime, interval, nor reference type.
The value of DecimalDigits when information is retrieved from an implementation row descriptor and the data type of the column is neither exact numeric, datetime, nor interval.
The value of ROW_COUNT retrieved by GetDiagField when the statement executed was not a ‹delete statement: searched›, an ‹update statement: searched›, an ‹insert statement›, or a ‹merge statement›.
The values of all fields in an item descriptor area not explicitly set by SetDescField.
The manner in which, following the execution of an SQL procedure statement by an SQL-server, diagnostic information is passed into the SQL-agent’s diagnostics area stack in the SQL-client.
